newsitem.title: UK: RUGBY UNION-WALLABIES OWE DEBT TO IN-FORM BURKE.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-WALLABIES OWE DEBT TO IN-FORM BURKE.

text.p: Australia put their European tour firmly back on track on Saturday with a 29-19 victory over Scotland which owed much to another fine kicking display from full-back Matt Burke.

Burke, who contributed 20 points in the 40-18 win over Italy, emerged with another 19 points after an impressive all-round effort which allowed a rebuilding Wallaby team to gloss over the problems of the past week.
With a lengthy list of injuries and critics sharpening their knives back home, the result was a comfort for coach Greg Smith although the performance was far from perfect.
Both sides did manage two tries, but Scotland were also unable to discover their rhythm for long periods and gave Burke the chance to kick five penalties and two conversions from nine attempts.
The 23-year-old from Sydney, the Wallabies' player of the year, had 14 points by half-time when Australia led 19-6 and by the end had taken his international points tally past 150 in his 20th test.

Until Daniel Herbert exploited gaps in the Scottish cover with 12 minutes left, the only other Wallaby scorer had been lock Warwick Waugh, only in the tour party as a replacement for injured Garrick Morgan.

Waugh was at the centre of a rolling maul, the Wallabies' most potent weapon during a sequence of damp matches in Scotland, which was eventually rewarded with a try after 14 minutes to the dismay of most of the 51,171 crowd.
Scottish full-back Rowen Shepherd kicked three penalties, but the home side found it difficult to make consistent headway against a Wallaby pack in which captain John Eales was outstanding.
Aside from Eales, the man of the match was probably Scotland's new captain Gregor Townsend whose elusive running made him a danger every time he received the ball.

Sadly for Scotland, it was not often enough to rouse his side to rare early-season heights. They did at least manage second-half tries from wings Kenny Logan and Tony Stanger, adjudged to have touched down in the corner in the last minute, ensuring the final score was less embarrassing than recent losses to the All Blacks and Springboks at the same time of year.

At least one Wallaby finished the day with mixed feelings. Flanker Owen Finegan earned himself the dubious distinction of being the first player in international rugby to be substituted for reasons other than injury, following the recent law change by the International Board.
He was replaced with 15 minutes left by ACT team mate Brett Robinson, but 100-cap winger David Campese stayed on the bench throughout.

Scotland - 15-Rowen Shepherd; 14-Tony Stanger, 13-Gregor Townsend, 12-Ronnie Eriksson, 11-Kenny Logan; 10-Craig Chalmers, 9-Gary Armstrong (18-Bryan Redpath, 76 mins); 8-Eric Peters, 7- Ian Smith, 6-Murray Wallace, 5-Doddie Weir, 4-Damian Cronin, 3- Barry Stewart, 2-Kevin McKenzie, 1-Dave Hilton.

Australia - 15-Matthew Burke; 14-Tim Horan, 13-Daniel Herbert, 12-Pat Howard, 11-Joe Roff; 10-David Knox, 9-Sam Payne; 8-Daniel Manu, 7-David Wilson, 6-Owen Finegan (19-Brett Robinson, 65), 5-John Eales, 4-Warwick Waugh, 3-Andrew Blades, 2-Michael Foley, 1-Richard Harry.
